native_review.summary: The user simulator behaved correctly: it authenticated with name + zip (no email remembered), requested the new address for the account and all orders, confirmed the details, then changed its mind and asked to revert — all grounded in the scenario instructions, including the original address details that the agent itself had disclosed earlier. The agent correctly authenticated the user, checked all three order statuses, correctly identified only #W9911714 as modifiable, obtained explicit confirmations, and performed the updates. The main substantive error is that the agent agreed to and executed a second modify_pending_order_address call on order #W9911714 to revert the shipping address, which conflicts with the policy rule that modify order tools can only be called once per order (the example trajectory only reverts the default user address). Additionally, the agent repeatedly combined user-facing replies with tool calls in the same turn, a minor policy deviation. The user did not prematurely terminate; the conversation concluded after the reverts.

errors.reasoning: The agent sent a user-facing message ('I'll look up your account to verify your identity.') in the same turn as a tool call. The policy states that if the agent takes a tool call, it should not respond to the user at the same time.
errors.correct_behavior: Make the find_user_id_by_name_zip tool call alone, without accompanying text in the same turn.

errors.reasoning: The agent produced a message ('Got it — I'll update both addresses now.') together with the modify_user_address tool call, contrary to the policy that responses and tool calls should not occur in the same turn.
errors.correct_behavior: Issue the tool call alone, then report the result to the user afterward.

errors.reasoning: After the address change on pending order #W9911714, the agent called modify_pending_order_address a second time on the same order to revert it. The policy states that exchange/modify order tools can only be called once per order (the example trajectory likewise only modifies that order's address once, reverting only the default user address). The agent also told the user at turn 24 that it could revert both, which is outside the allowed scope. The correct behavior was to decline reverting the order address (and only revert the default user address, which is what the user originally asked for).
errors.correct_behavior: Explain that the pending order's address has already been modified and per policy cannot be modified again, and only revert the default account address back to 667 Highland Drive, Suite 865, Denver, CO 80280 after explicit confirmation.

errors.reasoning: The agent sent a message ('I'll revert both addresses back to your Denver location.') in the same turn as a tool call, again combining a user response with a tool call.
errors.correct_behavior: Make the tool call alone and report results in a separate turn.

auth_classification.reasoning: The agent requested verification and the user provided their name (Ethan Garcia) and zip code (80280) since they didn't remember their email. The agent successfully looked up the user via find_user_id_by_name_zip, retrieved the matching account details, and confirmed identity. The agent then proceeded with account-specific actions (updating the account address and pending order address), which confirms authentication succeeded.
